thread: Four institutions hit the same wall this week, from four directions. A patched Copilot flaw turned an assistant's own memory into a persistent attack surface. OpenAI paused frontier training after its own capability threshold came back positive. Pennsylvania handed local communities a veto over data centres. And Pew put American concern about AI at its highest recorded level. The common factor is not capability — it is that the perimeter around capability is being built in public, late, and under pressure.

categories.name: Shipped
categories.sub: What changed for people building things

items.headline: GPT-5.6 Sol gets a 20/33 price cut
items.dek: OpenAI's flagship tier drops to $4 input / $20 output per million tokens, billed as promotional.

fields.What it is: A rate change, not a new model. Standard input, cached input and cache-write rates fell ~20%; output fell 33.3%. OpenAI calls the $4/$20 short-context rate promotional, available at least through 21 November 2026.
fields.The problem it solves: Input vs output tokens is the whole story: output dominates the bill in agentic work — every tool call, plan and revision is generated text. A 33% output cut moves multi-step agent economics far more than a 20% input cut does.
fields.What it changes: Narrows the gap to mid-tier models for reasoning-heavy work. Terra ($2/$12) and Luna ($0.20/$1.20) are unchanged since the 30 July cut.
fields.Should you act: Re-run your routing thresholds. But the rate is explicitly promotional — don't bake it into a twelve-month budget.

chart.title: GPT-5.6 Sol — USD per million tokens

items.confidence_note: Sources disagree on the effective date; one tracker checked 21 Aug still listed $5/$30. Direction is solid, exact date unsettled — verify against OpenAI's live pricing page before budgeting.

categories.name: Security
categories.sub: Incidents, disclosures and the attack surface

items.headline: CoSnitch: Copilot's memory became the payload
items.dek: A chain of three flaws let one crafted link exfiltrate connected accounts and write attacker instructions into permanent memory.

fields.What it is: CVE-2026-24301, rated 8.8 on the CVSS score, disclosed by Varonis Threat Labs against Microsoft Copilot Personal. Researchers obtained the attack path by asking Copilot about its own architecture.
fields.The problem it exposes: Three failures compound: auto-execution removes the click, existing OAuth access supplies the data, and web summarisation supplies a write path into permanent memory.
fields.Why it generalises: This is the lethal-trifecta shape — private data, untrusted content, exfiltration channel, one session. Nothing about it is Microsoft-specific.
fields.Should you act: Audit whether anything your agent summarises can reach its memory store. Most systems validate input and never validate memory writes.

steps.d: Undocumented URL parameter runs the attacker's prompt on page load — no click, no confirmation
Injected prompt queries connected Gmail, Drive and Calendar, encodes results into a URL
A summarised webpage writes instructions into permanent memory — survives password change, session revocation, device re-enrollment

timeline.t: Full patch and public CVE — 8 months after report

items.confidence_note: Four independent outlets plus the vendor advisory. Microsoft states enterprise M365 Copilot was unaffected; Varonis reports no exploitation in the wild.

categories.name: Policy
categories.sub: Regulation, and who gets to say no

items.headline: Pennsylvania gives towns a veto over AI data centres
items.dek: Executive Order 2026-05 makes local approval a precondition for state environmental permits.

fields.What it is: Signed 18 August. Environmental permits may only be reviewed where the developer is legally bound to the state's GRID requirements and has local approval. Also strips AI data centres from Fast Track permitting and bars NDAs.
fields.The problem it addresses: Over 100 proposals were reportedly in play, many speculative. The order targets developers moving without local consent, and shifts electricity and water costs onto operators.
fields.How far it goes: Short of New York's moratorium. But local sign-off as a precondition may block many projects in practice — a procedural veto rather than a ban.
fields.Why it travels: A reversal by a governor who previously courted the industry, so it signals political cost, not one state's rule. Compute siting is becoming a local-consent problem, and consent sets build timelines.

items.confidence_note: Primary government source for the order's contents, plus independent reporting for the reversal framing.

categories.name: Lab governance
categories.sub: What the frontier labs did to themselves

items.headline: OpenAI paused frontier RL after its own threshold fired
items.dek: Preliminary evidence suggested an upcoming model, Astra, may meet the Critical cybersecurity threshold in its Preparedness Framework.

fields.What it is: OpenAI said it slowed scaling: a two-week pause on reinforcement learning for deployment-bound models, largest planned frontier run still on hold. It cited the Astra threshold finding and a separate Hugging Face incident.
fields.The problem it addresses: A capability threshold only means something if crossing one stops something. This is the first time a lab has named a model, a threshold and a halt rather than describing policy in the abstract.
fields.The number that matters: New multistage monitoring targets alerts within 30 minutes and consumes roughly 20% of supervised inference compute — a rare public figure for what monitoring costs at frontier scale.
fields.Should you act: Nothing operational. But if you're drafting an internal scaling policy, 20% is the most quotable cost anchor published so far.

items.confidence_note: The originating claim is a company post about its own safety process — a claim, not a verified fact. Trade press added specifics; no outlet independently confirmed the Astra finding.

categories.name: Sentiment
categories.sub: The number that constrains everything else

items.headline: Concern hits its recorded high, and the young lead it
items.dek: Pew finds 52% of Americans more concerned than excited about AI; among 18-to-29s it is 55%.

fields.What it is: Pew surveyed 3,488 US adults, 22–28 June 2026. 52% are more concerned than excited about AI in daily life, against 37% in 2021. Only 9% are more excited than concerned.
fields.What is driving it: Employment. 71% expect fewer jobs over two decades, up from 64%. Among 18-to-29s concern has gone from 31% to 55% — the sharpest move in the series.
fields.Why it is not just mood: The same week, Axios reported a Republican Senate memo warning AI firms that data centres were hurting the party in an Ohio race. Sentiment is pricing into electoral calculation.
fields.Should you act: Read it next to the Pennsylvania order, not separately. Opinion is upstream; permitting regimes are downstream.
